def test_correct_bracketing():
    # Empty string is trivially balanced
    assert correct_bracketing("") is True

    # Simple balanced pair
    assert correct_bracketing("<>") is True

    # Single open bracket — never closed
    assert correct_bracketing("<") is False

    # Single close bracket with no opener
    assert correct_bracketing(">") is False

    # Closing before opening (wrong order) triggers negative depth
    assert correct_bracketing("><") is False

    # Nested brackets
    assert correct_bracketing("<<>>") is True

    # Deep nesting
    assert correct_bracketing("<<<>>>") is True

    # Sequential balanced pairs
    assert correct_bracketing("<><>") is True

    # Nested plus sequential
    assert correct_bracketing("<<>><<>") is True

    # Extra closers at end leaves depth negative path / nonzero depth
    assert correct_bracketing("<>>") is False

    # Extra opener at end leaves depth positive
    assert correct_bracketing("<<>") is False

    # Mismatched pattern where depth recovers but ends nonzero
    assert correct_bracketing("<><") is False

    # Longer mixed example
    assert correct_bracketing("<<><>>") is True

    # Negative depth occurs midway even though total counts match
    assert correct_bracketing("><<") is False

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_correct_bracketing()

# Unit test for function correct_bracketing
def test_correct_bracketing():
    # Valid bracketing cases
    assert correct_bracketing("") is True          # empty string is balanced
    assert correct_bracketing("<>") is True        # simple pair
    assert correct_bracketing("<<>>") is True      # nested pair
    assert correct_bracketing("<><>") is True      # sequential pairs
    assert correct_bracketing("<<><>>") is True    # mixed nesting
    assert correct_bracketing("<<<>>>") is True    # deep nesting

    # Invalid bracketing cases
    assert correct_bracketing("<") is False        # unclosed bracket
    assert correct_bracketing(">") is False        # close before open
    assert correct_bracketing("><") is False       # closes first
    assert correct_bracketing("<><") is False      # trailing unclosed
    assert correct_bracketing("<<>") is False      # unbalanced depth
    assert correct_bracketing("<><>>") is False    # extra closing
    assert correct_bracketing(">>>") is False      # all closing
    assert correct_bracketing("<<>>><") is False   # valid then unclosed
